analysis.title: DB CoTD: October: A (small) nightmare on Wall Street...
key_insights: October was a rotation out of tech and French risk into energy and core government bonds. Oil's +93.3% YTD gain (Brent) remains the dominant theme in the year-to-date table.

Oil led October gains: Brent +13.6% and WTI +15.2%, taking YTD gains to +93.3% and +81.3%. Brent ended the month at $117.64/bbl, close to its 2026 high. The report cites Houthi attacks, Hormuz disruption and fears of renewed US strikes on Iran after the midterms as keeping the risk premium rising.
European gas rose +43.6% in October to EUR 103.94/MWh, its highest since 2022.

Tech was the biggest drag as doubts about AI capex spread from semiconductors to the wider sector. The Philly semiconductor index fell -15.3% in October and -19% from 6 October to month-end. The Nasdaq lost -5.3%, its worst month since March 2025.
Alphabet's -12.64% post-results day was its worst on record.
The KOSPI (-14.7%) was the weakest of the major indices DB tracks. The Nikkei fell -5.3%.

Treasuries rebounded sharply. The 10yr yield hit a post-2002 high of 5.31% early in the month, then fell to 4.93%. Weaker risk sentiment and on-hold decisions from the Fed, ECB and BoJ restored the safe-haven bid. Treasuries returned +2.3%, their best month of 2026, but are still -0.5% YTD.
Gilts gained +2.6% in October. Bunds gained only +0.4% in USD terms because a weaker euro offset most of the rally.

France was the focus of European stress. The 10yr OAT-Bund spread reached 174bps on 22 October, its widest since November 2011, and the French 10yr yield hit 5.07%. OATs lost -1.7% and BTPs and EU sovereigns lost -0.5%.
The euro fell to 1.1160, its lowest since spring 2025, which hurt USD returns on all euro assets. EU HY lost -2.5% and European HY spreads widened +65bps to 370bps. European banks fell -11.7%.

Equities rotated beneath the headlines. The S&P 500 fell -0.9% while the equal-weighted index gained +5.0%. In USD, the DAX rose +0.9% and the STOXX 600 +0.5%, so Europe held up outside France and the periphery.
Losses elsewhere were broad. MSCI EM fell -8.0%, Brazil's Bovespa fell -14.3% after Lula's election win, and the Shanghai Composite lost -5.3% (-2.7% YTD).
Gold lost -6.8% and silver -18.7% in October, leaving both among the weakest assets YTD (-10.3% and -31.5%).
Even after the October selloff, the Philly semiconductor index remains +51.6% YTD.
